t: Section 3(a) of the Act of July 30, 1956 (70 Stat. 722; 16 U.S.C. 718b–1), is amended by striking out “Postmaster General” each place it appears therein and inserting in lieu thereof “Postal Service”.

fable.w: This is a purely technical amendment that substitutes one federal entity's name (Postal Service) for another (Postmaster General) in an existing statute. No tempting reading exists: there is no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government. Both entities named are inside the federal government.
fable.s: is amended by striking out “Postmaster General” each place it appears therein and inserting in lieu thereof “Postal Service”

qwen_block.w: This section is a purely technical amendment that updates the name of a federal entity from 'Postmaster General' to 'Postal Service'. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties. There is no mention of public hearings, advisory boards with non-federal members, or coordination with states or the public.
qwen_block.s: Section 3(a) of the Act of July 30, 1956 (70 Stat. 722; 16 U.S.C. 718b–1), is amended by striking out “Postmaster General” each place it appears therein and inserting in lieu thereof “Postal Service”.

opus.w: This is a technical amendment that replaces "Postmaster General" with "Postal Service" in an existing statute. Nothing in it brings states, tribes, the public, experts or companies into a federal decision. Swapping the name of one federal entity for another is not participation.
opus.b: 1. **Reasoning.** The only possible trap is that the Postal Service is now an independent establishment rather than an executive department, so you might ask whether it counts as "outside" the government. It doesn't matter here. The amendment just swaps one federal actor's name for another's. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue, so no outside party is involved in any federal decision.

It does not establish any advisory committees, public comment periods, consultations with states or tribes, or rights to sue. It involves no interaction with parties outside the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: Section 3(a) of the Act of July 30, 1956 (70 Stat. 722; 16 U.S.C. 718b–1), is amended by striking out “Postmaster General” each place it appears therein and inserting in lieu thereof “Postal Service”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that changing the name of an agency implies a change in how the public interacts with it, or that "Postal Service" implies public participation. However, this is merely a textual amendment updating a proper noun to reflect an organizational change. It does not create any new process for consultation, comment, or coordination with outside parties.
